name: HIEF grants for community-led nature protection and restoration
summary: Grants of GBP 5,000 to 20,000 for community-led projects that protect and restore nature across the Scottish Highlands and Islands, mainly for local non-profits and community bodies. Pure research and individual PhD work are excluded.

eligibility.rule: Show strong leadership, use an integrated bottom-up approach, involve communities and demonstrate positive impact
If over £1m annual income or non-local, evidence capacity need or local-community delivery impact
If over £1m annual income or non-local, have an informal discussion with HIEF before applying
If over £1m annual income or non-local, request at least 10% of the project budget from HIEF
Lead the project through the community or evidence full local-community support
Propose neither an individual PhD nor a specialist research study

calls.label: Late February - early March 2027 round

status.quote: The next grant deadline will be in late Feburary - early March 2027. Exact dates will be available on the HIEF website before the end of 2026.

calls.note: Next deadline expected late February to early March 2027; exact dates before end of 2026

applicant_types.quote: Local non-profit organisations, associations, clubs or unions, social co-operative enterprises and/or other local bodies, including research centres, are strongly encouraged to apply for grants.

geography.quote: The HIEF will support projects throughout the Scottish Highlands and Islands

access.quote: get in touch with [email protected] for a discussion prior to applying

window.quote: The next grant deadline will be in late Feburary - early March 2027.

amount.quote: HIEF awards grants between £5,000 and £20,000 for community-led projects that protect and restore nature in the Scottish Highlands & Islands.

eligibility.quote: All applicants must display strong and effective leadership and emphasise an integrated, bottom-up approach, consulting with, mobilising and involving local communities and demonstrating positive community impact.
The applicant can evidence i) the need for their capacity building to support local communities or ii) how they will work with local communities to deliver tangible impact
The organisation has had an informal discussion with [email protected] prior to applying
The HIEF funding requested constitutes at least 10% of the overall project budget
There must be clear, identifiable environmental benefit(s)
The project must be either community-led or evidence full support from local communities.
Individual PhD applications and specialist research studies will not be considered for funding.
Pure research will not be considered for funding.
